To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the natural amphetamine-like cathedrins (cathinone, norephedrin, cathine) have a unique effect on intracellular signaling in leukocyte subsets, whereas the botanical khat (C. edulis Forsk.) extract has a distinct effect on intracellular signal transduction.
Cathinone, the amphetamine-like cathedrone derivative, and its derivatives cathine and the ephedrine-like norephedrin, induce a distinct signal transduction profile in human leukocytes.

cathinone, amphetamine-like derivatives, and the khat-extract (Catha eduliss Forsk.) induce unique signaling profiles in human leukocytes, which may be of relevance for their pharmacologic and toxicological properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pharmacological effects of khat and amphetamine-like compounds, which have been used for centuries in the Horn of Africa and Yemen, and more recently in the Western world as recreational drugs.

the pharmacology of the khat plant (Catha edilis) and its main psychoactive constituent cathinone (2-amino-1-phenylpropan-1-one), as well as the cathinone-related compounds cathine (2-amino 1-phenyl-1-propanol) and norephinephrine (2-amino-N-methyl-1-phenylethanamine).
the effects of amphetamine-like substances on the immune system and their possible immunomodulatory effects, which may have clinical implications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cathinone and cathine have immunomodulatory effects on human cells of the immune systems.
the effects of khat and cathinone are not the same and that khat extract has a more pronounced effect than cathinone.
the khat-extract, cathinone, and norephendrine all induce different effects on immune cell signaling and proliferation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the khat-extract, cathinone, and the cathinone-derivatives cathine and noraephedrine all induce unique signaling profiles in immune cells, and that the cathinone and derivatives reduce phosphorylation of c-cbl, ERK, p38, and p53.
khat extract induces an inflammatory response in immune cells, whereas cathinone and its derivatives have immunomodulating effects.
khat-extract and amphetamine-like compounds induce distinct signaling profiles in leukocyte subsets, and that khat-extracts induce immunomodulatory effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the single cell analysis of intracellular signaling in immune cells is an effective tool in the elucidation of pharmacological effects of amphetamides and botanical extracts.

single cell analyses of immune cells could provide valuable information on the pharmacologic effects of complex botanical extracts, and further could help to unravel mechanism(s) of actions of complex botanical extracts and amphetamine derivatives.
khat and its constituents have the potential to modulate the immune response.
